purpose: Close the verified-source gap for the 24 previously uncovered UMS departments and seed role-level professional knowledge. This is a living PROD knowledge baseline, not a claim that every role is fully mastered.

knowledge_points: Use watch time and audience retention as primary attention signals.
Compare high-performing and weak Shorts to isolate repeatable creative differences.
Track viewed-versus-swiped-away behavior, likes, comments and remixes as complementary signals.
Treat the first 30 seconds as a measurable introduction gate for long-form video.
Use dips, spikes and top moments to diagnose abandonment, rewatching and sustained interest.
Align title and thumbnail promise with opening content to reduce expectation mismatch.
Test multiple creative variants continuously to reduce creative fatigue.
Use strong early hooks, high visual contrast and platform safe zones for Stories/Reels.
Use controlled A/B testing before declaring creative superiority.
Retrieve publisher-deposited bibliographic metadata, funding, licenses, updates, ORCID/ROR identifiers and abstracts through the public REST API.
Use DOI metadata and post-publication update signals to improve source verification and retraction awareness.
Treat abstracts as potentially copyrighted even when metadata is broadly reusable.
Use structured metadata properties for accurate, consistent resource identification, citation and retrieval.
Track schema version explicitly; observed current minor version is 4.7.
Prefer persistent identifiers and provenance-preserving metadata over free-text citation memory.
Use the public API for findable DOI metadata without authentication where appropriate.
Preserve provenance and state when harvesting metadata.
Use JSON:API-compatible structured retrieval rather than scraping citation text when possible.

sources.publisher: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
knowledge_points: Evaluate story for originality, forward motion, coherent beginning/middle/end and emotional journey.
Evaluate voice for distinctiveness and originality rather than imitation.
Evaluate characters for vividness and distinct individual voices.

sources.publisher: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
knowledge_points: Use real Fellowship-winning scripts as reference material for professional screenplay structure and execution.
Separate script-format reference from creative-quality judgment.
Compare genre, scene construction, dialogue density and pacing across successful scripts rather than memorizing a single template.
Model branching narrative with text-first markup, choices, state and logic.
Keep narrative middleware separable from the game/UI layer.
Compile narrative to an intermediate representation for validation and deterministic playback.
Represent nonlinear stories as visible branching passages.
Use variables and conditional logic to model stateful narrative.
Treat story format as a runtime choice with distinct features and constraints.
Construct palettes from complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary and monochromatic relationships.
Extract palette information from reference imagery to preserve visual coherence.
Separate color harmony selection from accessibility validation.
Measure foreground/background contrast rather than judging readability by eye alone.
Check palettes against color-vision deficiencies and WCAG contrast targets.
Preserve brand intent while maintaining readable contrast in text and graphical UI.
Treat digital human creation, animation, capture and runtime use as separate pipeline stages.
Use high-fidelity identity, rig, hair/groom, LOD and animation concepts as explicit continuity dimensions.
Support both creator-authored synthetic characters and authorized performer-based identities with separate provenance.
Represent performer likeness as a dedicated identity asset rather than transient frame similarity.
Capture neutral and teeth poses; include additional left/right views where the capture workflow requires them.
Use the same class of device for identity and performance capture when the solver requires consistent capture characteristics.
Support real-time and offline animation from mono video, depth data and audio sources.
Separate ingest, calibration, solve, animation export and automation stages.
Use scripting APIs to scale repeatable capture processing instead of manual-only workflows.
Prefer even diffused lighting with minimal harsh shadows, blur or camera shake for performance capture.
Maintain sufficient face/body pixel detail and avoid heavy compression.
Stabilize head-mounted capture relative to the performer and treat lighting/capture quality as solver inputs, not cosmetic concerns.
Represent speech synthesis intent with structured language, voice, emphasis, phoneme, prosody, break and say-as controls.
Document supported languages and accents for each voice.
Treat prosodic control as language- and voice-dependent rather than assuming identical rendering across engines.
Benchmark speech systems on content consistency and speaker similarity, not subjective likeness alone.
Support multilingual TTS, voice design, expressive control and authorized voice cloning as distinct capabilities.
Keep model/license/runtime evaluation separate from consent and voice-rights authorization.
Track unified speech and singing pipelines covering TTS, SVS, VC, SVC, singing editing and style conversion.
Treat melody control, prosody control and speaker identity as separate evaluation axes.
Use reproducible open research implementations as benchmark candidates, not automatic production dependencies.
Design lighting intentionally for location/studio, subject shape, mood, texture and separation.
Treat fixture capability, position, softness, direction, contrast and practical constraints as a system.
Build reusable lighting setups from measured techniques instead of arbitrary stylistic presets.
Use Structure-from-Motion to recover camera poses and sparse geometry before dense reconstruction.
Use Multi-View Stereo and fusion to produce dense point clouds and meshes.
Track camera models, calibration, rigs, datasets and reconstruction diagnostics explicitly.
Separate guided image capture from model reconstruction.
Use a stateful capture session and hand captured images to photogrammetry reconstruction only after capture completes.
Treat capture completeness and reconstruction as independently observable pipeline stages.
Represent immersive video from multiple texture and depth views for constrained 6DoF viewing.
Track common test conditions, encoder guidelines and test models as benchmark references.
Treat volumetric/immersive delivery as coded-view reconstruction rather than ordinary 2D video.
Track immersive capture, post, mastering, spatial audio, live production and playback as separate disciplines.
Use platform-native spatial preview and immersive-media workflows for validation.
Treat 6DoF/spatial experiences as interaction and presence problems, not merely wide-FOV video.
Use 2D, isometric, perspective and symmetry guides to construct consistent spatial artwork.
Separate structural drawing assistance from stylistic brush rendering.
Use perspective vanishing points and drawing assist to enforce environment/object coherence.
Construct and transform artwork on explicit perspective planes.
Use snapping, smart guides and grid structure for repeatable spatial alignment.
Keep object dimensions/properties editable while preserving perspective relationships.
Animate typography at layer, source-text and per-character levels.
Use selectors and animators for controlled motion rather than flattening text prematurely.
Treat titles, lower thirds, credits and kinetic type as distinct motion-design patterns.
Use behaviors, keyframes or a combination for text animation.
Separate whole-object motion from per-character sequencing and parameter animation.
Build reusable motion presets only after validating timing and readability.
Represent cinematics with level sequences, tracks, cameras, keyframes and bound actors.
Use nonlinear editing semantics for animation and cinematic state.
Keep sequence data separate from scene actor instances for reusable control.
Use cine camera actors and explicit transform keyframes for controlled camera movement.
Pilot cameras to validate framing from the actual shot viewpoint.
Separate camera motion intent, framing and timing so each can be reviewed independently.
Use professional editing, effects, color and distributed-processing documentation as workflow references.
Model collaborative editorial and shared-storage workflows explicitly.
Treat transcript-assisted and multicam automation as accelerators that still require editorial review.
Use a unified reference for editing, color, VFX/motion graphics, audio post and finishing.
Track version-specific codec and feature support before assuming interchange compatibility.
Keep editorial, Fusion, Fairlight and color operations separately testable even in one application.
Represent editorial cut information with clips, timing, tracks, transitions, markers and metadata.
Reference external media rather than embedding it into the timeline interchange object.
Use adapters/plugins to bridge proprietary NLE formats while preserving timeline semantics.
Use Grease Pencil for traditional 2D animation, cut-out work, motion graphics and storyboarding in 3D space.
Separate strokes, keyframes, materials, modifiers, lighting and effects.
Use frame-based animation with explicit keyframe control and pressure-aware drawing inputs.
Use FPS, holds and onion-skin settings as explicit animation timing controls.
Treat 12 unique drawings/sec as a common drawn-animation cadence and 24 fps as a higher-smoothness target where appropriate.
Validate motion rhythm by playback rather than assuming more frames always improves quality.
Use animation, brushes, layers, masks, HDR, command-line and render features as separate pipeline components.
Preserve editability through layers/masks before render/export.
Use logs and deterministic export settings for reproducible animation troubleshooting.
Model mocap as setup, system calibration, performer calibration, capture, cleanup and export.
Distinguish optical, inertial and markerless capture modalities.
Treat synchronization, reconstruction, labeling, filtering, skeleton solving and retargeting as independently testable stages.
Use qualified stunt coordination for planning, setup, performance, rehearsal, modification and equipment decisions.
Require performer consent and appropriately trained personnel for stunt activity.
Treat explosives, animals and specialized hazards as separate safety domains requiring qualified handlers/technicians.
Use data-oriented fragments/entities/archetypes for scalable crowd state.
Separate simulation data from behavior logic and rendering representation.
Use LOD/avoidance/debugging systems to manage scale and diagnose crowd behavior.
Manage perceived loudness consistently across production and delivery.
Use normalization intentionally rather than uncontrolled peak matching.
Treat dialogue intelligibility as a measurable delivery concern alongside artistic intent.
Separate dialogue editing, ADR, sound effects, routing, buses, EQ/dynamics, reverb, automation, panning, mix and final delivery.
Use dedicated tracks/layers and channel mapping for clean post-production organization.
Treat repair, design, mixing and mastering as distinct stages with different quality checks.
Design adaptive audio that reacts to game/application state.
Profile and audition audio while the application runs.
Keep authoring, runtime integration, mixing and platform delivery as separate responsibilities.
Treat MIDI 2.0 as an extension of MIDI 1.0 with backward compatibility rather than a wholesale replacement.
Use MIDI-CI for capability negotiation and UMP for modern protocol transport.
Separate note/event representation, profiles, property exchange and device capability discovery.
Use MusicXML/SMuFL as interoperable notation foundations and track MNX as an emerging format.
Preserve instrument, notation, microtonal and technique metadata where supported.
Track specification roadmaps and gaps explicitly instead of assuming notation round-trip parity.
Design immersive music from session setup through panning, vocal placement, monitoring and master rendering.
Build efficient session layouts before spatial mixing.
Validate headphone rendering and final master creation as explicit delivery stages.
Treat stem separation as source separation over spectral and temporal characteristics.
Keep extracted vocals/instruments editable as normal audio clips for remix, arrangement and processing.
Prefer local/offline-capable workflows when cost/privacy requirements favor them.
Use phonemizers, resamplers, MIDI editing, pitch/vibrato controls and voicebanks as explicit singing-synthesis layers.
Support multiple synthesis backends rather than hard-coding one singer engine.
Treat singing synthesis and DAW mixing as separate responsibilities.
Use music segments, playlists/switch containers and explicit transition rules for adaptive scoring.
Model source, destination and optional bridge/transition segments.
Use transition matrices and fallback rules to keep state changes musically coherent.
Integrate cameras, animation, lights, objects and events on a real-time cinematic timeline.
Use Sequencer as a nonlinear control surface for interactive and cinematic state.
Keep authored cinematic logic compatible with runtime event/state integration.

expected_coverage_after_merge.note: Zero department-level source gaps does not mean deep role mastery. Role-level section coverage remains separately measured.
